name: Aman Canal Grande, Venice
positioning: Palazzo Papadopoli hotel on the Grand Canal in Venice's San Polo district, which Aman calls Aman Venice
best_for: Travelers who want to stay in a historic palazzo with frescoed suites
Guests who want to arrive by boat on the Grand Canal

facts.text: Aman partnered with the Arrivabene family, who still live on the top floors of the palazzo.
The Sansovino Suite has a fireplace by the 16th-century architect Jacopo d'Antonio Sansovino.
Each bedroom is set in one of the palazzo's original rooms, so each is unique.
Arva is the hotel's Italian restaurant, with dishes such as Fassona beef carpaccio, rabbit cappelletti pasta and fish stew sourced from the Rialto market.
Sunday brunch is served in the gardens beside the Grand Canal, with dishes such as lobster Benedict and hazelnut pancakes.
Arva and The Bar are open to both Aman guests and non-residents.
The spa offers holistic therapies, some using Aman's natural skincare line.
Aman lists the transfer from Marco Polo Airport as 50 minutes by boat.

highlights.text: The Alcova Tiepolo Suite lets guests sleep beneath Giovanni Battista Tiepolo's cherub-filled frescos.
Guests can arrive by boat from under the Rialto Bridge to the palazzo's private jetty on the Grand Canal.
The hotel is in San Polo, on the other side of the Rialto Bridge from San Marco.

considerations.text: WhataHotel notes ultra-luxury pricing that reflects the hotel's exclusive positioning.
The airport transfer is by boat, which Aman lists as 50 minutes from Marco Polo Airport.
The spa has three treatment rooms, so it is a small spa.

sources.title: Condé Nast Traveler: Aman Venice review
